knowledge_type_note: Named mating pattern (D). Philidor's Legacy names the specific queen-sacrifice delivery, not every smothered mate; sources sometimes use the terms interchangeably.
definition_short: A knight mates a king that is completely surrounded by its own pieces.
definition_long:
The king is hemmed in on every side by its own men, so only a knight — which jumps — can reach it. The classic delivery, known as Philidor's Legacy, runs Qg8+ (a queen sacrifice on g8 or b8 forcing the rook to capture) followed by Nf7#, with the rook now blocking the last flight square.

The mechanism depends on DOUBLE CHECK earlier in the sequence: the knight checks from f7 or h6 with the queen also checking, so the defender cannot capture or interpose and must move the king into the corner.

history.notes: Descriptive pattern name of long, largely anonymous usage.

preconditions: The enemy king's flight squares are all occupied by its own pieces
A friendly knight can reach a square giving check
indicators_for: The king is in the corner with rook and pawns adjacent
A queen sacrifice is available to fill the last escape square
indicators_against: A flight square is empty or can be vacated

exceptions: If any surrounding piece can move away with tempo, the mate evaporates.
limitations: Reported only on an actual mate. The pattern without the mate is a king that happens to be surrounded, which is a description rather than a mating pattern. Fires on none of the 788 shipped positions and on the constructed Philidor pattern.

TYPICAL_CONFIDENCE RAISED medium -> high, 2026-09-02, and the reason is the schema's own definition of the field: 'how confidently this concept can normally be asserted ONCE ITS PRECONDITIONS HOLD'. This concept's recognition is MECHANICAL and its knowledge type already carries a high ceiling, so once the preconditions hold there is nothing left to be uncertain about - a stalemate is a stalemate, and a fork this base reports is one findMotifs() found, which ARCHITECTURE.md makes the authority and forbids second-guessing. 'Medium' was the default across 32 rule and motif records regardless of detectability, and it was found by measuring what the API reports against what each record permits: twelve concepts were reporting ABOVE their own record. The fix was to make each record its own ceiling in cap(), which then required the records that were wrong to be corrected rather than silently overruled.

Verified 2026-09-02. Both of this record's indicators_against - "A flight square is empty or can be vacated" and "The knight's square is defended" - describe positions that are not mate, and the detector only speaks when the position IS mate: findMotifs() computes `const mated = !theirMoves.length && inCheck(after, them)` from the move generator's own reply list. If a flight square existed, theirMoves would not be empty; if the knight could be taken, the same. Both conditions are unreachable rather than unguarded, which is a different and better answer than a guard would be.

examples.note: The classical picture, given as the MOVE that makes it rather than the position it leaves: Ng5-f7 mate against a king on h8 whose own rook on g8 and pawns on g7 and h7 occupy every flight square. Recorded as a move because this concept is a move concept - the record says 'reported only on an actual mate, because the pattern without the mate is a king that happens to be surrounded', and a position alone cannot carry that. Paired with the identical position with the h-pawn on h6, where Nf7 is a check and the king has h7.

tablebase.note: PROVEN: checkmate true. The pattern and the mate coincide here, which is what the record requires before the name is used.

counterexamples.note: The pattern without the mate, which is this record's own phrase for it: a knight checking a king boxed in by its own rook and pawn, where the h-pawn has moved to h6 and h7 is free. Nf7+ is a check and nothing more. Paired with the identical position with the pawn on h7, which is mate in the classical picture.

tablebase.note: The PAIRED position - pawns on g7 and h7 - is a proven mate, checkmate true. This one, with the pawn on h6, is not: the king has h7.

by_level.beginner: The king is boxed in by its own pieces, so the knight — the only piece that can jump — delivers mate.
by_level.intermediate: Smothered mate: every escape square is occupied by the king's own men.
by_level.advanced: Smothered mate. The Philidor's Legacy delivery uses a double check and a queen sacrifice to fill the last flight square.

beginner_words: boxed in by its own pieces
